picked.t: Two Ho Chi Minh City students win iPhone 17s for frequent bus travel
picked.body: The awards were presented Friday by the Ho Chi Minh City Public Transport Management Center, based on data from its payment and identification system. The center identified 10 students with the highest number of valid bus trips between Oct. 1 and 15. Tran Thanh Luong, a student at the University of Transport in Ho Chi Minh City, topped the ranking and received an iPhone 17 with 256 GB of storage. The other nine students were selected through a lucky draw. Le Quy, a student at the College of Radio and Television II, won the second iPhone 17 256 GB, provided by another sponsor. The remaining students received shopping vouchers worth VND1-2 million each. "I’ve taken the bus about 200 to 300 times (over Oct. 1-15)," Luong said. He regularly travels by bus to university and his part-time job. He also uses the journeys to observe transport management and operations, the field he is studying. "I never imagined that riding the bus could lead to winning an iPhone," Quy said, adding that buses are a convenient way for students to get around. Le Hoan, deputy director of the center, said this was the first time it had organized such a program. The initiative aims to encourage students and young people to use public buses and help ease traffic congestion. The center plans to continue it. Ho Chi Minh City has offered free rides on 134 public bus routes since July 1. These routes have carried more than 40 million passengers since, nearly 50% more than during the same period last year.

picked.t: Vietnam's top leader begins official visit to Japan
picked.body: During the visit, the Vietnamese leader is expected to meet Japan's Emperor and Empress, Prime Minister, and the presidents of both houses of parliament. He will also meet leaders of economic organizations and major corporations, attend and deliver a speech at the Vietnam-Japan Public-Private Forum on Economic and Science-Technology Cooperation, and visit a high-tech enterprise. The Vietnamese delegation includes Politburo members and Party Central Committee secretaries Nguyen Duy Ngoc, chairman of the Party Central Committee's Commission for Organization, and Le Minh Tri, chairman of the Commission for Internal Affairs. Other Politburo members joining the trip are General Phan Van Giang, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense; General Luong Tam Quang, Minister of Public Security; Le Hoai Trung, Minister of Foreign Affairs; Tran Duc Thang, Secretary of the Hanoi Party Committee; and Tran Luu Quang, Secretary of the Ho Chi Minh City Party Committee. The delegation also comprises Party Central Committee Members Nguyen Hai Ninh, Chief of the Party Central Committee Office; Ngo Van Tuan, Minister of Finance; Le Manh Hung, Minister of Industry and Trade; Vu Hai Quan, Minister of Science and Technology; and Trinh Viet Hung, Minister of Agriculture and Environment. Deputy Foreign Minister Nguyen Minh Vu said the visit holds strategic significance in three key areas. First, the two nations will establish an overarching strategic vision for bilateral relations in a new era, with leaders jointly identifying long-term cooperation priorities across various sectors to meet mutual development needs. Second, Vietnam and Japan will move beyond conventional economic, trade, and investment cooperation toward deeper economic integration. This shift will place greater emphasis on partnership, co-creation, and strengthening each country's economic autonomy and resilience. Third, the visit will provide momentum for breakthroughs in science, technology, innovation, and the transformation of development models. Japan brings strengths in advanced technology, capital, management experience, and manufacturing, while Vietnam offers a young workforce, a dynamic market, significant growth potential, and a strong commitment to promoting innovation. Vietnam and Japan established diplomatic relations in 1973 and upgraded ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2023. Japan is currently Vietnam's largest provider of official development assistance (ODA), its top labor cooperation partner, third-largest investor, and fourth-largest tourism and trading partner. Bilateral trade reached US$43.7 billion in the first nine months this year, up 15% year-on-year. Trade turnover had reached $51.43 billion in 2025. The Vietnamese community in Japan numbers nearly 700,000, featuring a growing proportion of intellectuals and highly skilled professionals. Currently, around 7,000 Vietnamese IT engineers are working in the country.

picked.t: New pedestrian overpasses set to transform downtown Ho Chi Minh City's riverfront
picked.body: Vehicles travel along Ton Duc Thang Street near Me Linh Square. Photo by Nguyen The Duong One pedestrian bridge will be built at the intersection of Ton Duc Thang and Nguyen Hue streets, directly in front of the Majestic Saigon Hotel. The second bridge will be located at the intersection of Thai Van Lung and Ton Duc Thang streets, in front of The Landmark building, nearly 1km away. Between these two upcoming bridges lies the Bach Dang Wharf Park. Stretching along the Saigon River, the park already attracts large numbers of residents and tourists for recreation and sightseeing every day. With a the nipa palm-shaped pedestrian bridge across the river expected to be completed next February, officially connecting the city center with the Thu Thiem New Urban Area, visitor numbers in this area are expected to surge. Construction barriers now line both sides of Ton Duc Thang Street as workers lay the foundations for the pedestrian bridge extending from Nguyen Hue Street. Great Wealth Trading and Services Co. Ltd. is developing the project under a build-transfer (BT) contract that requires no financial contribution from the city. The two overpasses carry an estimated cost of VND88 billion (US$3.3 million). The developer proposed the infrastructure update and is fully financing the construction through corporate capital and other legitimate funding sources.
